concepts.name: Types of emergency, National Emergency effects and Articles 358-359
concepts.description: The three emergencies in brief and the effects of a National Emergency on Centre-State relations, legislative tenure, finance and Fundamental Rights.
concepts.idea: A National Emergency turns the federal system unitary in practice, with Article 358 suspending Article 19 automatically and Article 359 suspending enforcement of specified rights by order.
concepts.rule: The Constitution provides National Emergency (Article 352; war, external aggression or armed rebellion), President's Rule (Article 356) and Financial Emergency (Article 360); the President proclaims all three. A National Emergency needs approval by both Houses by a special majority within one month and continues in six-month steps, while President's Rule and Financial Emergency need a simple majority within two months. During a National Emergency the Centre may direct States on any matter, Parliament may legislate on State List subjects (laws lapse six months after the Emergency ends), the Lok Sabha and Assemblies may be extended by one year at a time (not beyond six months after cessation) and revenue distribution may be modified. Article 358 automatically suspends Article 19 only on war or external aggression, and Article 359 suspends enforcement of specified rights by Presidential Order but never of Articles 20 and 21; after the 44th Amendment only Emergency-related laws are protected.
concepts.example: An Emergency proclaimed on armed rebellion does not suspend Article 19, but the President may still suspend enforcement of other specified rights, never of Article 21.

questions.q: A proclamation of emergency has to be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months by a simple majority. Once so approved it continues until the President revokes it; no fixed outer limit applies and no periodic renewal is needed. Which proclamation is described?
o: President's Rule under Article 356, which can run for up to three years at most
National Emergency under Article 352, proclaimed on the ground of war
National Emergency under Article 352, proclaimed on the ground of armed rebellion
questions.e: Only the Financial Emergency (Article 360) is approved by simple majority within two months and then continues indefinitely till revoked (Laxmikanth p.271).
w: President's Rule also needs a simple majority within two months, but it runs six months at a time and cannot exceed three years.
A National Emergency needs a special majority within one month and renewal every six months.
The ground does not matter: any National Emergency needs a special majority and six-monthly renewal.
tr: same approval rule as President's Rule

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about proclamations of emergency:

1. A National Emergency proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament by a special majority within one month.
2. A proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by both Houses within two months by a simple majority.
3. An approved Financial Emergency lapses unless Parliament renews it every six months.
4. An approved National Emergency lasts six months at a time and may be continued indefinitely by repeated six-monthly approvals.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.260-261 gives one month and a special majority. Statement 2 is correct: A proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by both Houses within two months by a simple majority (Laxmikanth p.265). Statement 3 is incorrect: it continues indefinitely until revoked, with no renewal (Laxmikanth p.271). Statement 4 is correct: periodic approval was added by the 44th Amendment (Laxmikanth p.260).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.260
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.260
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.260
tr: renewal belongs to NE, not FE

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the three emergencies:

1. A Financial Emergency brings the financial affairs of the States under Union control.
2. The ground for President's Rule is the failure of constitutional machinery in a State.
3. A Financial Emergency can be proclaimed when the financial stability or credit of India is threatened.
4. Article 360 is the provision under which President's Rule is imposed.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A Financial Emergency brings the financial affairs of the States under Union control (Laxmikanth p.272). Statement 2 is correct: The ground for President's Rule is the failure of constitutional machinery in a State (Laxmikanth p.265). Statement 3 is correct: Article 360 (Laxmikanth p.271). Statement 4 is incorrect: President's Rule is under Article 356; Article 360 is the Financial Emergency (Laxmikanth p.259). So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about duration and revocation of emergencies:

1. The Lok Sabha has no role in the revocation of a National Emergency, which the President decides on his own.
2. President's Rule and Financial Emergency are each revoked by the President by a subsequent proclamation.
3. A proclamation of Financial Emergency needs approval by both Houses by a simple majority within two months.
4. President's Rule can be extended up to a maximum of two years, in steps of six months, with Parliament's approval.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the President must revoke it if the Lok Sabha passes a resolution disapproving its continuation (Laxmikanth p.261). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.266 and p.271; no parliamentary approval is needed. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.271. Statement 4 is incorrect: The ceiling is three years, in six-month steps (Laxmikanth p.265).
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.261
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.261
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.261

questions.q: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 substituted which expression for 'internal disturbance' as a ground for proclaiming a National Emergency?
questions.e: Article 352 now reads war, external aggression or armed rebellion; 'internal disturbance' was dropped as too vague (Laxmikanth p.260).
w: Failure of constitutional machinery is the ground for President's Rule under Article 356.
'Breakdown of law and order' was never the substitute wording in Article 352.
Threat to financial stability is the ground for a Financial Emergency under Article 360.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the effects of emergencies:

1. A National Emergency gives the Constitution a strong unitary tilt, the Centre gaining control over State powers.
2. Under President's Rule the State government is dismissed or suspended and the Governor administers the State on behalf of the Centre.
3. Both a National Emergency proclamation (after the 44th Amendment) and President's Rule (as laid down in the Bommai case, 1994) are open to judicial review.
4. A proclamation of President's Rule is issued by the Governor on behalf of the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.259, p.262. Statement 2 is correct: Under President's Rule the State government is dismissed or suspended and the Governor administers the State on behalf of the Centre (Laxmikanth p.266). Statement 3 is correct: the 44th Amendment deleted the 38th Amendment's bar; Bommai laid down reviewability (Laxmikanth p.260, 269). Statement 4 is incorrect: all three emergencies are proclaimed by the President.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.259
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.259
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.259

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Under Article 359 the Fundamental Rights as such are not suspended during a National Emergency; only their enforcement is.
Statement-II: A Presidential Order under Article 359 may extend to the whole of the country or to only a part of it.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the rights remain theoretically alive and only the right to seek a remedy is suspended (Laxmikanth p.263). Statement-II is correct: the suspension order may extend to the whole or any part of the country (p.263). The territorial reach of an Order does not explain why the rights themselves survive, so II does not explain I.
w: Rejected: the area covered by the Order has no bearing on whether the rights themselves are suspended.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, so the pair is not half-correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct: only the enforcement of the rights is suspended.

questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It has been proclaimed three times: 1962, 1971 and 1975 (Laxmikanth p.264). Statement 2 is incorrect: Laxmikanth p.268 gives more than 125 occasions. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.272. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.259.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.264

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about National Emergency:

1. In normal times the Centre's executive directions to a State are limited to specified matters, but during a National Emergency they extend to any matter.
2. Parliament can legislate on State List subjects during a National Emergency.
3. The extension of the Lok Sabha's term may continue up to one year after the Emergency has ceased to operate.
4. According to Laxmikanth, the financial modification made during a National Emergency ceases six months after the Emergency ends.

Statement 4 is incorrect: it continues till the end of the financial year in which the Emergency ceases (Laxmikanth p.262). So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

Consider the following statements about legislative consequences of a National Emergency:

1. Parliament may confer powers and impose duties, for carrying out laws made under its extended jurisdiction, on State authorities but not on the Centre or its officers.
2. While a National Emergency operates, the President can issue ordinances on State List subjects if Parliament is not in session.
3. According to Laxmikanth, the 42nd Amendment confined the executive and legislative consequences of an Emergency to the State in which it is in operation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: such powers and duties may be conferred on the Centre or its officers and authorities (Laxmikanth p.262). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.262. Statement 3 is incorrect: it extended them to any other State as well (Laxmikanth p.262).
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.262
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.262

questions.q: During a National Emergency the Lok Sabha's normal term of five years can be extended by a law of Parliament
questions.a: by one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases to operate

Consider the following statements about the effects of a National Emergency on the States:

1. While a National Emergency operates, Parliament can extend the normal tenure of a State Legislative Assembly by one year at a time.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Laws made by Parliament on State subjects during a National Emergency become inoperative six months after the Emergency ceases.
Statement-II: State governments stand suspended while a National Emergency is in operation.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 358:

1. Articles 358 and 359 govern the effect of a National Emergency on Fundamental Rights, and Article 358 automatically suspends the six freedoms of Article 19.
2. Article 358 suspends Article 19 on whichever ground the National Emergency is declared, including armed rebellion.
3. While Article 19 is suspended, restricting laws and executive action cannot be challenged on that ground, and after the 44th Amendment this shield covers only Emergency-related laws and the executive action under them.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.262. Statement 2 is incorrect: after the 44th Amendment it operates only on war or external aggression (Laxmikanth p.263). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.263.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.262
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.262

questions.q:
Pair each entry in List-I with the correct entry in List-II.

List-I
A. Approval by both Houses within one month by a special majority
B. Maximum duration of three years
C. Continuance until revoked, without renewal
D. Automatic suspension of the six freedoms of Article 19

List-II
1. Article 356
2. Article 360
3. Article 352
4. Article 358
questions.e: A National Emergency (Article 352) needs one-month special-majority approval; President's Rule (Article 356) has a three-year ceiling; a Financial Emergency (Article 360) continues until revoked; Article 358 suspends Article 19 automatically (Laxmikanth p.260-263, 265, 271).
w: B and C are interchanged: President's Rule carries the three-year ceiling, the Financial Emergency has no limit.
A and B are interchanged: the one-month special majority belongs to Article 352.
C and D are interchanged: Article 360 is the open-ended emergency and Article 358 the automatic suspension.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 359:

1. Under Article 359 the Fundamental Rights named in the Presidential Order are themselves suspended for its duration.
2. A Presidential Order under Article 359 cannot take away the right to move courts for the protection of Articles 20 and 21.
3. Only those Fundamental Rights specifically mentioned in the Presidential Order can have their enforcement suspended.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: only their enforcement is suspended; the rights remain alive (Laxmikanth p.263). Statement 2 is correct: 44th Amendment (Laxmikanth p.263). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.263.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.263
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.263
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.263

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a safeguard against misuse of the National Emergency provisions introduced by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978?
questions.a: The power to confine a National Emergency to a specified part of the country
o: The power to confine a National Emergency to a specified part of the country
A requirement of the written recommendation of the Cabinet before the President proclaims the Emergency
Reduction of the time allowed for parliamentary approval from two months to one month after proclamation
Approval of the proclamation by a special majority of each House instead of a simple majority
questions.e: The power to confine a National Emergency to a part of India came from the 42nd Amendment, 1976; the other three are 44th Amendment safeguards (Laxmikanth p.260-261).
w: The Cabinet recommendation requirement was added by the 44th Amendment.
The approval period was cut from two months to one by the 44th Amendment.
The special-majority rule was added by the 44th Amendment; earlier a simple majority sufficed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency, according to Laxmikanth:

1. When a National Emergency ends, Article 19 revives automatically and laws inconsistent with it cease to have effect to that extent.
2. Once the Emergency has ended, actions taken under it can be challenged and a remedy is available.
3. Article 359 gives protection from challenge to all laws made during the Emergency, whether or not they relate to it.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.263. Statement 2 is incorrect: no remedy lies for anything done during the Emergency, even after it expires (Laxmikanth p.263). Statement 3 is incorrect: after the 44th Amendment only Emergency-related laws and the executive action under them are protected (Laxmikanth p.263). So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.

concepts.name: Articles 358 and 359 compared, the three Emergencies of 1962-75 and President's Rule
concepts.description: Differences between Articles 358 and 359, the instances of National Emergency, the Shah Commission, judicial review and the consequences of President's Rule.
concepts.idea: Article 358 is automatic, Article 19 only and external-emergency only, while Article 359 needs an order and reaches any right except Articles 20 and 21; President's Rule replaces the State executive and legislature with Union control.
concepts.rule: Article 358 is automatic, covers Article 19 only, operates only on war or external aggression, lasts for the whole Emergency and extends to the entire country; Article 359 needs a Presidential Order, covers specified rights other than Articles 20 and 21, operates on any Article 352 Emergency, lasts for the period in the order and may be confined to a part. Emergencies were proclaimed in October 1962 (Chinese aggression in NEFA, in force till January 1968), December 1971 (Pakistan's attack) and June 1975 (internal disturbance); the last two were revoked in March 1977. The Shah Commission did not justify the 1975 proclamation. The 38th Amendment barred judicial review, the 44th repealed the bar and Minerva Mills (1980) allows challenge for malafides, extraneous facts or absurdity. Under President's Rule the Council of Ministers is dismissed, the Governor administers for the President, the Assembly is dissolved or suspended, and Parliament (Article 357) makes laws that survive the proclamation until repealed or re-enacted.
concepts.example: A law made by the President for a State under President's Rule remains in force after the Rule ends until the reconstituted Legislature repeals or amends it.

questions.q: Article 358 does not operate when a National Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of
questions.e: After the 44th Amendment Article 19 stands suspended only on war or external aggression, not armed rebellion; Article 359 has no such exception (Laxmikanth p.263-264).
w: War is a ground on which Article 358 does operate.
External aggression is a ground on which Article 358 does operate.
A proclamation on imminent danger of external aggression is still a proclamation on that ground, so Article 358 applies.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing Article 358 and Article 359:

1. Article 358 operates only on the strength of a Presidential Order, while Article 359 suspends rights automatically.
2. Article 358 suspends Article 19 for the entire duration of the Emergency, while Article 359 suspends enforcement for the period specified in the Presidential Order.
3. Article 358 concerns only Article 19, whereas Article 359 can reach any Fundamental Right except those under Articles 20 and 21.
4. Article 358 extends to the entire country, whereas Article 359 may extend to the whole country or only a part of it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the reverse is true: Article 358 is automatic and Article 359 needs a Presidential Order (Laxmikanth p.264). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.264. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.263-264. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.264.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.264
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.264
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.264

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Article 356 is also known as State Emergency or Constitutional Emergency.
2. According to Laxmikanth, beyond one year President's Rule can be extended only if a National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held.
3. The 44th Amendment leaves the enforcement of Article 21 open to suspension by a Presidential Order during war, so personal liberty stays within the executive's reach.

Statement 3 is incorrect: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended at all (Laxmikanth p.263). Statement 4 is incorrect: three times: 1962, 1971, 1975 (Laxmikanth p.264). So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A fresh proclamation of National Emergency was not needed when war with Pakistan broke out in 1965.
Statement-II: The National Emergency proclaimed in October 1962 remained in force till January 1968.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about proclamations of National Emergency:

1. The first National Emergency outlived the 1962 war and made a fresh proclamation unnecessary at the time of the 1965 war with Pakistan.
2. The first National Emergency was revoked soon after the fighting with China ended in 1962.
3. The second National Emergency was proclaimed in December 1971 on external aggression after Pakistan's attack and, per Laxmikanth, was revoked in March 1977.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: it stayed in force till January 1968 (Laxmikanth p.264). Statement 2 is incorrect: it remained in force from October 1962 till January 1968 (Laxmikanth p.264). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.264.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.264
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.264
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.264

questions.q: The third National Emergency, proclaimed in June 1975, rested on which ground?
questions.a: Internal disturbance, as Article 352 then read
o: Internal disturbance, as Article 352 then read
Armed rebellion, which Article 352 then listed beside war and external aggression
External aggression, after an attack by Pakistan on the western border
War, arising out of the Indo-Pak conflict of that year
questions.e: The 1975 proclamation was made on the ground of 'internal disturbance', the pre-1978 wording; the 44th Amendment later substituted 'armed rebellion' (Laxmikanth p.260, 264).
w: 'Armed rebellion' replaced 'internal disturbance' only through the 44th Amendment in 1978.
External aggression was the ground of the 1962 and 1971 proclamations.
War was not the ground; the 1971 proclamation was the one linked to the Indo-Pak conflict.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Emergency of 1975:

1. The 1975 proclamation was made during the Prime Ministership of Indira Gandhi.
2. It was marked by allegations of curtailed civil liberties and misuse of preventive detention laws.
3. The Shah Commission, appointed after the 1977 change of government, upheld the necessity of the 1975 proclamation.
4. The 1975 proclamation was revoked in 1977.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The 1975 proclamation was made during the Prime Ministership of Indira Gandhi (Laxmikanth p.260, 264). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.264 records widespread criticism of misuse of Emergency powers. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Commission did not justify the declaration (Laxmikanth p.265). Statement 4 is correct: in March 1977 (Laxmikanth p.264).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.260
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.260

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the use of Article 356:

1. In 1977 the Janata government under Morarji Desai imposed President's Rule in nine Congress-ruled States, on the ground that their Assemblies no longer represented the electorate.
2. In the Bommai case (1994) the Supreme Court held that the State Assembly should be dissolved only after Parliament has approved the proclamation, and until then can only be suspended.
3. In the Bommai case the Court laid the burden on the Centre to prove that relevant material exists to justify President's Rule.
4. President's Rule was first imposed in a State in 1959.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.268. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.269. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.269. Statement 4 is incorrect: Laxmikanth p.268: first imposed in Punjab in 1951. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about judicial review of a National Emergency:

1. The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 retained the 38th Amendment's bar on judicial review of a National Emergency proclamation.
2. A proclamation of National Emergency can be challenged on grounds such as malafide intention or reliance on wholly extraneous or irrelevant material.
3. In Minerva Mills (1980) the Supreme Court treated a National Emergency proclamation as a political question beyond judicial examination.
4. The 38th Amendment Act, 1975 sought to make the proclamation of National Emergency immune from judicial review.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the 44th Amendment deleted that bar, restoring judicial scrutiny (Laxmikanth p.260). Statement 2 is correct: Minerva Mills (Laxmikanth p.260). Statement 3 is incorrect: it held the proclamation can be challenged on defined grounds. Statement 4 is correct: The 38th Amendment Act, 1975 sought to make the proclamation of National Emergency immune from judicial review (Laxmikanth p.260).
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.113
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.113
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.113

questions.q: A challenge to a National Emergency proclamation before the Supreme Court was allowed, in the case decided in 1980, on which of the following grounds?
questions.a: Malafide intention, reliance on wholly irrelevant facts, or an absurd or perverse decision
o: Malafide intention, reliance on wholly irrelevant facts, or an absurd or perverse decision
Failure to consult the Chief Ministers of the States, or to take the Governors' reports on law and order
Approval by the Lok Sabha with a simple majority, or by the Rajya Sabha without a division of votes
That war was stated as the ground, when armed rebellion, also a valid ground under Article 352, could have been stated
questions.e: Minerva Mills allows challenge on grounds of malafide, wholly extraneous or irrelevant facts, or an absurd or perverse decision (Laxmikanth p.260).
w: The Constitution requires no consultation with Chief Ministers or Governors' reports for a National Emergency; they are not grounds in the case.
Approval by the wrong majority is a procedural matter, not one of the grounds laid down in the case.
Both war and armed rebellion are valid grounds under Article 352, so choosing between them is not a ground of challenge.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule:

1. Under President's Rule the State Legislative Assembly may be dissolved or kept under suspended animation.
2. Suspended animation means fresh elections follow, whereas dissolution keeps the Assembly intact but inactive.
3. The Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister continues in office, with the Governor acting merely as an adviser.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Statement 2 is incorrect: dissolution implies fresh elections; suspended animation keeps the Assembly intact but inactive (Laxmikanth p.274 note 8). Statement 3 is incorrect: the Council of Ministers is dismissed and the Governor carries on the administration on behalf of the President (Laxmikanth p.266).
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.266

questions.q:

Consider the following statements about the consequences of President's Rule:

questions.q:
Pair each event in List-I with its cause or date in List-II.

List-I
A. First National Emergency, October 1962
B. Second National Emergency, December 1971
C. Third National Emergency, June 1975
D. Revocation of the 1971 and 1975 proclamations

List-II

2. Chinese aggression in the North-East Frontier Agency

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about legislative powers during President's Rule:

1. Parliament can delegate the power to make laws for the State to the President, who may specify another authority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.266. Statement 2 is incorrect: the expenditure awaits the sanction of Parliament (Laxmikanth p.266). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.266. Statement 4 is incorrect: they can confer powers and impose duties on the Centre or its officers and authorities (Laxmikanth p.266).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.266

questions.q: Article 357 of the Constitution deals with
questions.a: exercise of legislative powers under a proclamation issued under Article 356
o: exercise of legislative powers under a proclamation issued under Article 356
suspension of the provisions of Article 19 during Emergencies
the duty of the Union to protect the States against external aggression and internal disturbance
application of the provisions on distribution of revenues while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation

That is Article 355.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Articles 358 and 359 were left untouched by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
2. The 1975 National Emergency was associated with allegations of misuse of preventive detention laws.
3. An Article 359 order must remain in force for the entire duration of the Emergency.
4. Under President's Rule the State bureaucracy is replaced by Central officers, ending the State's day-to-day administration.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: both were narrowed by it (Laxmikanth p.263). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.264 records widespread criticism of the misuse of Emergency powers. Statement 3 is incorrect: it may run for the Emergency or a shorter period specified in the order (Laxmikanth p.264). Statement 4 is incorrect: day-to-day administration continues through the State bureaucracy. So 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only two' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

concepts.name: National Emergency versus President's Rule, Financial Emergency and the 44th Amendment safeguards
concepts.description: Comparison of the emergencies, the Financial Emergency under Article 360, the summary table and the safeguards of the 44th Amendment.
concepts.idea: The three emergencies differ in ground, approval, duration, revocation and effect on rights, and the 44th Amendment added the Cabinet, special-majority and time-limit safeguards.
concepts.rule: National Emergency can cover the country or a part and is proclaimed on the Cabinet's written recommendation; President's Rule is imposed only on a State and on the Governor's report or otherwise. In a National Emergency Parliament cannot delegate State List lawmaking, in President's Rule it can (President's Acts); a National Emergency can be revoked by a Lok Sabha resolution while President's Rule is revoked by the President on his own. A Financial Emergency (Article 360) needs a simple-majority approval within two months, continues until revoked, and has never been proclaimed. The 44th Amendment required the written Cabinet recommendation, cut approval time to one month with a special majority, and limited President's Rule beyond one year to when a National Emergency is in force and the Election Commission certifies; Bommai (1994) made Article 356 reviewable.
concepts.example: Beyond one year, President's Rule needs both a National Emergency and an Election Commission certificate.

questions.q: President's Rule can be continued, by successive approvals of Parliament, up to a maximum of
questions.a: three years, in steps of six months
o: three years, in steps of six months
five years, in steps of one year
two years, in steps of three months
no fixed maximum, as with a National Emergency
questions.e: President's Rule starts for six months and may be extended in six-month steps to a ceiling of three years, unlike a National Emergency (Laxmikanth p.265, 267).
w: Five years applied only to Punjab by a special amendment in 1991; the general ceiling is three years.
Extensions are in steps of six months, not three, and the ceiling is three years.
A National Emergency has no maximum; President's Rule does.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing National Emergency and President's Rule:

1. A National Emergency is proclaimed on the Cabinet's written recommendation, whereas for President's Rule the President may act on the Governor's report or otherwise.
2. A National Emergency may cover the entire country or specific States, whereas President's Rule is imposed only on specific State(s).
3. A National Emergency rests on failure of constitutional machinery in a State, whereas President's Rule rests on war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
4. Both the proclamation of a National Emergency and that of President's Rule need the written recommendation of the Cabinet.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A National Emergency is proclaimed on the Cabinet's written recommendation, whereas for President's Rule the President may act on the Governor's report or otherwise (Laxmikanth p.260, 265). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.260, 267 (Table 17.1, row 5). Statement 3 is incorrect: The grounds are the other way round (Laxmikanth p.267, Table 17.1). Statement 4 is incorrect: the Cabinet requirement is for a National Emergency; the President may impose President's Rule on a Governor's report or otherwise (Laxmikanth p.260, 265).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.260
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.260
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.260

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. A National Emergency needs the President to be satisfied that a grave emergency exists from war, external aggression or armed rebellion, whereas President's Rule can rest on the Governor's report or other information.
2. Neither President's Rule nor a Financial Emergency directly suspends Fundamental Rights.
3. A resolution approving a Financial Emergency requires a special majority of each House.
4. Under Article 365, a State's failure to comply with a Central direction cannot be treated as a failure of constitutional machinery.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A National Emergency needs the President to be satisfied that a grave emergency exists from war, external aggression or armed rebellion, whereas President's Rule can rest on the Governor's report or other information (Laxmikanth p.260, 265). Statement 2 is correct: Neither President's Rule nor a Financial Emergency directly suspends Fundamental Rights (Laxmikanth p.268). Statement 3 is incorrect: a simple majority suffices (Laxmikanth p.271). Statement 4 is incorrect: the President may hold that such a situation has arisen (Laxmikanth p.265). So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Like a National Emergency, President's Rule can be continued indefinitely by Parliament's approval every six months.
2. According to Laxmikanth, during a National Emergency Parliament makes laws on State List subjects by itself and cannot delegate the power.
3. During President's Rule Parliament can delegate law-making for the State to the President or another authority, and such laws are called President's Acts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: President's Rule has a three-year ceiling (Laxmikanth p.267). Statement 2 is correct: according to Laxmikanth p.267 Parliament can make State List laws during a National Emergency only by itself, not delegating to any other body. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.267.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.267
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.267
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.267

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct way in which President's Rule can be revoked?
questions.a: By the President at any time, through a later proclamation needing no approval of Parliament
o: By the President at any time, through a later proclamation needing no approval of Parliament
By a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by a simple majority, as is done for a National Emergency
By a resolution of the State Legislative Assembly concerned, passed by a two-thirds majority of its members
By the President only after both Houses pass resolutions of disapproval by a special majority of each House
questions.e: Laxmikanth p.266 and Table 17.1 (p.268): President's Rule is revoked by the President on his own; there is no Lok Sabha-resolution route (that exists for a National Emergency).
w: The Lok Sabha-resolution route belongs to a National Emergency only.
The Constitution gives the State Assembly no such power; it may even be dissolved or suspended.
No parliamentary resolution of disapproval is needed for revocation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. President's Rule leaves all Fundamental Rights, including the right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32, unaffected.
2. During a National Emergency the enforcement of all Fundamental Rights, including those under Articles 20 and 21, can be suspended.
3. A National Emergency can be revoked by a simple-majority resolution of the Lok Sabha, whereas President's Rule is revoked by the President on his own.
4. During a National Emergency the State government continues to function, whereas under President's Rule it is dismissed or suspended and the Governor takes over the executive.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.268. Statement 2 is incorrect: Articles 20 and 21 remain enforceable (Laxmikanth p.263). Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.268 (Table 17.1, row 8). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.262, 266, 267.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.268
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.268
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.268

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Laws made for a State under President's Rule, on a delegation from Parliament, are known as President's Acts.
Statement-II: According to Laxmikanth, during a National Emergency Parliament cannot delegate its power to legislate on State List subjects to any other body.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Laws made for a State under President's Rule, on a delegation from Parliament, are known as President's Acts (Laxmikanth p.267). Statement-II is correct: according to Laxmikanth p.267. The non-delegation rule belongs to National Emergency and does not explain the name given to President's Rule laws.
w: Statement-II concerns the other emergency and gives no reason for the name in Statement-I.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Financial Emergency:

1. Article 360 permits a Financial Emergency if the financial stability or credit of India, or of any part of its territory, is threatened.
2. A proclamation of Financial Emergency must be approved by both Houses within two months of its issue.
3. The resolution approving a Financial Emergency needs only a simple majority of members present and voting.
4. Once approved, a Financial Emergency continues until revoked, with no fixed outer time limit and no periodic renewal.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.271. Statement 2 is correct: Article 360(2); Laxmikanth p.271. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.271. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.271.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.271
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.271

questions.q: If the Lok Sabha is dissolved during the two months allowed for approving a Financial Emergency, the proclamation
questions.a: survives for 30 days after the new Lok Sabha first meets, provided the Rajya Sabha has meanwhile approved it
o: survives for 30 days after the new Lok Sabha first meets, provided the Rajya Sabha has meanwhile approved it
lapses at once, because only the Lok Sabha is competent to approve a proclamation of Financial Emergency
survives until 60 days from the first sitting of the reconstituted Lok Sabha, with no need of Rajya Sabha approval
survives indefinitely until the President obtains the approval of the Rajya Sabha alone, with no outer time limit
questions.e: The 30-day rule with prior Rajya Sabha approval applies (Laxmikanth p.271).
w: Approval by the Rajya Sabha in the interim keeps the proclamation alive; the Lok Sabha is not the only House that approves.
The period is 30 days and Rajya Sabha approval is mandatory.
The new Lok Sabha must still approve within 30 days of its first sitting; there is no open-ended survival.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Financial Emergency:

1. Where the Lok Sabha is dissolved within the approval period, a Financial Emergency stays alive for 30 days after the new House first meets, if the Rajya Sabha has already approved it.
2. A Financial Emergency may be ended by the President through a later proclamation that Parliament need not approve.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.271. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.271. Statement 3 is incorrect: A direction may require the reduction of the salaries and allowances of persons serving the Union and of the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts (Laxmikanth p.272). Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.271.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.271

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the revocation of a National Emergency:

1. A written notice from one-tenth of the total membership of the Lok Sabha obliges a special sitting to consider a resolution disapproving the continuation of a National Emergency.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A written notice from one-tenth of the total membership of the Lok Sabha obliges a special sitting to consider a resolution disapproving the continuation of a National Emergency (Laxmikanth p.261). 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements from a summary comparison of the emergencies:

1. A Financial Emergency requires approval by both Houses by a special majority within one month.
2. The grounds are war, external aggression or armed rebellion for a National Emergency, failure of constitutional machinery for President's Rule, and a threat to financial stability or credit for a Financial Emergency.
3. A National Emergency, like President's Rule, is limited to a maximum of three years.
4. According to Laxmikanth, President's Rule has been imposed on more than 125 occasions since 1950, whereas a Financial Emergency has never been proclaimed.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it needs a simple majority within two months (Laxmikanth p.271). Statement 2 is correct: summary; Laxmikanth p.259. Statement 3 is incorrect: a National Emergency has no maximum, renewed every six months (Laxmikanth p.267). Statement 4 is correct: According to Laxmikanth, President's Rule has been imposed on more than 125 occasions since 1950, whereas a Financial Emergency has never been proclaimed (Laxmikanth p.268, 272).
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.115

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the emergencies and the Fundamental Rights of citizens is correct?
questions.a: Neither President's Rule nor a Financial Emergency directly suspends the Fundamental Rights of citizens
o: Neither President's Rule nor a Financial Emergency directly suspends the Fundamental Rights of citizens
A Financial Emergency suspends the right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 for enforcing the rights
President's Rule suspends Article 19 automatically on proclamation, in the way a National Emergency does

Articles 358 and 359 operate during a National Emergency, not during President's Rule.

Consider the following statements:

1. Whatever the ground of a National Emergency, the right to move courts to enforce Articles 20 and 21 stays available.
2. Article 19 stands suspended on all three grounds of National Emergency, including armed rebellion.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: 44th Amendment (Laxmikanth p.263). w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.263

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 made a written recommendation of the Cabinet necessary for proclaiming a National Emergency.
Statement-II: In 1975 the proclamation was advised by the Prime Minister without consulting the Cabinet, which was informed only afterwards.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I

Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 made a written recommendation of the Cabinet necessary for proclaiming a National Emergency (Laxmikanth p.260). Statement-II is correct: (Laxmikanth p.260) and is why the safeguard was introduced.
w: Laxmikanth states the 1975 episode as the reason for the safeguard, so II does explain I.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 44th Amendment and President's Rule:

1. The 44th Amendment raised the period for parliamentary approval of a National Emergency from one month to two months.
2. President's Rule runs for at most six months at a time, with an overall ceiling of three years.
3. According to Laxmikanth, extending President's Rule beyond one year needs both a National Emergency in operation and an Election Commission certificate that elections cannot be held.
4. In S.R. Bommai (1994) the Supreme Court held that the President's satisfaction under Article 356 is subject to judicial review.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it reduced the period from two months to one (Laxmikanth p.260). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth p.265. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth p.266. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth p.269.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.260
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.260
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.260

questions.q:
Match the Articles of the Constitution in List-I with the subject each deals with in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 352
B. Article 356
C. Article 360
D. Article 365

List-II
1. Failure of a State to follow a Central direction
2. Danger to the financial stability or credit of the country
3. Security threat from war, external aggression or armed rebellion
4. Failure of constitutional machinery in a State, on a Governor's report or otherwise
questions.e: Article 352 rests on war, external aggression or armed rebellion; Article 356 on failure of constitutional machinery; Article 360 on a threat to financial stability or credit; Article 365 lets non-compliance with a Central direction be treated as such a failure (Laxmikanth p.259, 265).
w: A and B are interchanged: Article 352 is the security ground.
C and D are interchanged: Article 360 is the financial ground.
B and D are interchanged: Article 356 is the general failure ground; Article 365 is the non-compliance ground.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Dr B.R. Ambedkar said that the Financial Emergency article follows the pattern of the Government of India Act, 1935.
2. A Financial Emergency is meant to deal with extraordinary fiscal crises such as collapse of public finances or severe macroeconomic instability.
3. The balance-of-payments crisis of 1991 led the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: he said it follows the pattern of the National Recovery Act of the USA, 1933 (Laxmikanth p.272). Statement 2 is correct: A Financial Emergency is meant to deal with extraordinary fiscal crises such as collapse of public finances or severe macroeconomic instability. Statement 3 is incorrect: none has been proclaimed so far, although there was a financial crisis in 1991 (Laxmikanth p.272).
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.272
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.272
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.272

questions.q: A National Emergency can be proclaimed by the President only after he/she has received
questions.a: a written recommendation from the Cabinet
o: a written recommendation from the Cabinet
a report from the Governor of the State concerned
a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by a special majority
the advice of the Prime Minister alone
questions.e: The 44th Amendment made the written recommendation of the Cabinet a condition, so that the Prime Minister alone cannot decide (Laxmikanth p.260).
w: A Governor's report is relevant to President's Rule, and even there it is not compulsory.
Parliament approves a proclamation only after it is made, not before.
The 44th Amendment ended the possibility of the Prime Minister alone deciding.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the duration of President's Rule:

1. The 68th Amendment Act, 1991 permitted the President's Rule imposed on Punjab in May 1987 to run for five years, according to Laxmikanth.
2. The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 raised the period of one approval of President's Rule from six months to one year, and this still holds.
3. Beyond one year, President's Rule can be extended on the strength of the Election Commission's certificate, even without a National Emergency.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth p.274, note 7. Statement 2 is incorrect: the 44th Amendment reduced it again to six months (Laxmikanth p.274, note 6). Statement 3 is incorrect: both conditions are needed (Laxmikanth p.266). So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
